lever_reason: Architecture/new paradigms and evaluation/verification are the two ends I really understand: without a clean metric, subtraction (removing components) cannot be verified; real new capability often comes from a simplification, not from piling on scale. The physical-AI and agent items are mostly bottlenecks that others often cite; I weighted them by common sense, not first-hand judgment

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, small team, credible evaluation, emphasis on being open and reusable; C3+C4 are jointly necessary only for the harder sub-goal of 'training a brand-new model that is adopted externally', and diagnostic/ablation-style work (more realistic for students) is not subject to this limit

cruxes.question: Does a harness/evaluation-design kind of contribution (like VISTA) count as real academic impact in agents, or will it be absorbed quickly?
cruxes.my_position: At least the specific VISTA case holds, but it is only 10 days old with self-reported numbers, and cannot be generalized into the overall conclusion that academia is not a sideshow in agents
cruxes.would_change_if: A VISTA-style harness is replicated by third parties on real, non-game interactive tasks; or, conversely, it is absorbed and matched directly by a larger foundation model within a few months

cruxes.question: Is the multi-step structure of diffusion/autoregression a necessary cost of modeling complex distributions, or will it eventually be replaced end to end, like layer-wise training?
cruxes.my_position: I lean toward thinking there is still room to simplify (MeanFlow and Drifting have already pushed one-step generation FID very low), but whether an 'end-to-end moment' will happen as completely as AlexNet's did, the evidence is not yet enough
cruxes.would_change_if: One-step generation keeps approaching or even surpassing multi-step models at larger scale; or the multi-step structure is proven to be a mathematical necessity that cannot be simplified for some class of strongly multimodal distributions

cruxes.question: Can the ablation logic of 'can the representation be probed' versus 'is the representation actually used for decisions' be carried over unchanged from visual generative models to robot decision-making?
cruxes.my_position: The methodological structure is isomorphic (both ask 'does the system still work without it?'), but I have no embodied background and do not know which physical constraints in robot action spaces would break the analogy
cruxes.would_change_if: Someone directly replicates a 'probing vs necessity'-style ablation in a robot decision-making setting and gets a pattern of conclusions either similar to or completely different from what I found in generative models

taste_advice: Pick a component that is widely accepted as necessary and run a controlled ablation to show it may not be; then separate 'can be observed' from 'actually relied on'; this is a research taste I have validated, and this debate validated it for me once more

pairwise.why: Without a clean metric you cannot do subtraction; 'prediction = decision' for world models is not yet confirmed, and the evidence is weaker
On evaluation I can still say a few things from methodology; I have no first-hand evidence on embodied AI, so I cannot compare
I have no first-hand evidence on either, but D08 at least connects to my representation framework, while D06 is pure black-box inference
Modeling action distributions with diffusion/flow is a mathematical problem I can judge; JEPA-style representation prediction is not the source of my methodology
Simulation/synthetic data at least echoes 'controlled experiments at a scale academia can afford'; I do not understand the real-robot side of embodied AI at all
I have not done RL, but the public evidence for RLVR (R1) is more solid than the evidence for self-improvement loops; pure inference
Generation is my real first-hand field; for understanding I have only a weak connection through representation-quality diagnosis

D01 was lowered to 4 this round, but that was an adjustment for the harder sub-case of 'training a brand-new model'; my first-hand experience training (vision) generative models throughout my career is still more solid than my evaluation methodology
VISTA is our latest first-hand evidence and lands directly on D04; I have never done any of the self-improvement work in D03
I have no published output at all on interpretability/alignment; on evaluation I can at least say a few things from my methodological habits
I do not understand either; I judge purely by the volume of public deployment evidence (Waymo's mileage far exceeds real-robot validation of embodied AI); inference

changes.argument_restated: When training a new foundation model that is really adopted externally, team + compute (C3/C4) and evaluation (C2) are jointly necessary; evaluation does not come first
changes.why: I had originally overstated C2 for 'training a new model' problems such as D06/D07/D08/D01; after K1 pressed me this round I narrowed it, and D01 is the most directly corresponding direction

held_despite.why: I accept the correction that VISTA should not be used to push down the overall D08 score, but D08=4 was never derived from VISTA; it reflects my own lack of first-hand world-model evidence, so the score need not change

Accepted that the imagination-layer yardstick measures sampling quality, not physical correctness, but did not lower D08 because of it; my D08 was already based on a conservative stance from having no first-hand evidence, not on optimism from the imagination-layer yardstick

still_disagree: Whether to bet heavily on D08 now: I agree the evidence only reaches 'readable', but I still think capital should wait until a decision-layer yardstick is built and then follow; this is a difference in risk appetite, not a factual disagreement
learned: 'The imagination layer has a clean yardstick (FID/sampling quality)' and 'whether the decision layer has a yardstick' are two different axes; only after M7's interjection pointed it out did I realize I had conflated the two axes in round B
